story_type: onboard window camera: capsule reentry plasma, parachutes open, splashdown splash on the glass
hook: The view from a capsule falling home from the Moon.
narration: This is the view out the window of a capsule falling home from the Moon, at nearly twenty five thousand miles an hour.
NASA's Orion had flown more than one point four million miles, around the Moon and back, with no crew aboard.
Then it hit the top of the atmosphere.
The air in front of it was squeezed so hard it turned into glowing plasma, about five thousand degrees Fahrenheit.
That is about half as hot as the surface of the Sun, just outside the glass.
In about twenty minutes, the air slowed it from twenty five thousand miles an hour to about twenty.
First, two small drogue chutes pulled out.
Then three giant main parachutes opened above the window.
And the ocean came up to meet it.
outcome: Orion splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, west of Baja California, and came home safe.

location_card.place: Pacific Ocean, west of Baja California

title: Falling from the Moon, seen from inside
description:
On Dec. 11, 2022, NASA's uncrewed Orion spacecraft reentered Earth's atmosphere at nearly 25,000 mph after a 1.4 million-mile Artemis I mission around the Moon. A camera at its window recorded the plasma, the parachutes and the splashdown west of Baja California.
